title: The ü sound
howTo: Say a long "ee". Without moving your tongue, push your lips forward into a tight "oo" circle.
trap: English speakers slide the tongue back and say "oo", turning Tür (door) into "tour".

title: The ö sound
howTo: Say "ay" as in "day" without the glide. Keep the tongue there and round your lips as for "oh".
trap: It usually comes out as "oh" or "er", so schön (beautiful) becomes schon (already).

title: The ä sound
howTo: Open e like in "bed". In long syllables, hold it.
trap: Reading it as the a in "cat".

title: The soft ch (ich-Laut)
howTo: Whisper the y of "yes" forcefully, like a cat hissing softly. Used after e, i, ä, ö, ü, ei, eu and consonants.
trap: Saying "sh" (ich becomes "ish") or "k" (ich becomes "ick").

title: The hard ch (ach-Laut)
howTo: Like the end of Scottish "loch": air rubbing at the back of the mouth. Used after a, o, u, au.
trap: Replacing it with k, so Nacht (night) becomes nackt (naked).

title: The German r
howTo: Raise the back of the tongue toward the soft palate, as if gargling very lightly. The tongue tip stays down behind the lower teeth.
trap: The English r with a curled tongue tip is the single most noticeable sign of an English accent.

title: Vocalic r (-er, -r)
howTo: After a vowel or at the end of a word, r becomes a short open "uh". Mutter sounds close to "mutta".
trap: Pronouncing a full American r at the end of der, hier, Wasser.

title: z = ts
howTo: A t immediately followed by s, like the end of "cats", even at the start of a word.
trap: Using the buzzing English z.

title: w = v
howTo: Lower lip lightly touching the upper teeth, voice on. Exactly English v.
trap: Rounding the lips into an English w.

title: v = f
howTo: In native German words v is pronounced f.
trap: Saying English v in Vater, von, viel.

title: s before a vowel
howTo: s before a vowel is voiced like English z.
trap: Hissing a sharp s in Sonne, sieben, Rose.

title: sp and st at the start
howTo: At the start of a word or word part, sp and st sound like "shp" and "sht".
trap: Saying a plain s like in English "sport".

title: sch
howTo: Exactly English sh, with lips slightly rounded.
trap: Few problems here, but do not confuse it with the soft ch.

title: Final devoicing
howTo: b, d, g at the end of a word or syllable lose their voice and become p, t, k.
trap: Voicing the final consonant like English: Hund said with a real d.

title: -ig at the end
howTo: -ig at the end of a word ends in the soft ch sound.
trap: Saying "ig" or "ik".

title: ei versus ie
howTo: Say the second letter: ei sounds like English "eye", ie sounds like "ee".
trap: Mixing them up when reading, so Wein (wine) becomes Wien (Vienna).

title: eu and äu
howTo: Both sound like "oy" in "boy".
trap: Reading eu as "you".

title: au
howTo: Like "ow" in "how".
trap: Reading it as the "aw" in "saw".

title: Long versus short vowels
howTo: A vowel is long before h, when doubled, or before a single consonant. It is short before a double consonant. Length changes meaning.
trap: English vowels do not contrast length the same way, so Staat (state) and Stadt (city) blur together.

title: The glottal stop
howTo: Words and word parts that start with a vowel get a tiny catch in the throat before them. German does not link words the way English does.
trap: Running words together: "am Abend" said as "a-mabend".

title: pf
howTo: Close the lips for p, then release straight into f.
trap: Dropping the p and saying only f.

title: ng
howTo: One nasal sound, as in English "singer", with no g after it.
trap: Adding a g like in English "finger".

title: Final -e
howTo: A final e is always spoken as a short, relaxed "uh".
trap: Dropping it, so bitte becomes "bit".

title: qu
howTo: k followed by v.
trap: Saying "kw".
